question: Should the repair lane roll out these fail-closed authorization and final-request mutation guards as one coordinated change?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but it deliberately trades automation availability for stronger stale-state protection across several authoritative write paths; only maintainers can accept that rollout boundary.

options.title: Approve coordinated rollout
options.body: Land the current design after required checks pass, accepting conservative retries when freshness or credentials cannot be proven.

options.title: Split operational rollout
options.body: Merge mutation authorization first and stage state-token renewal or receipt-publication changes separately to reduce blast radius.

options.title: Keep the draft paused
options.body: Leave the PR open until maintainers want the broader fail-closed behavior in production repair workflows.

recommendation.title: Approve coordinated rollout
recommendation.body: Land the current design after required checks pass, accepting conservative retries when freshness or credentials cannot be proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged foundation and current-main feature history most directly connect this person to the authorization model and its rollout tradeoffs.
